title: Duke visits Scott's mother about going to Europe
summary: Ellington visits Scott's mother, she leaves the decision to Scott, and he decides to stay.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I talked to Duke. I talked to him, and he talked to me just like a brother. I'll never forget what he

said. He says, I'll tell you what, Scottie, I'll come up to you and speak to your mother tomorrow and explain to her about what it's all about. I says, well, I wouldn't leave her without her consent, because she was my heart.

I found out that Duke was very fond of his mother, too, in Washington, D.C. and he brought her home and everything before she died, and she died before he did, too. Well, the next morning, Duke was up there at 157 W. 123rd Street, right on 7th Avenue, that big house there. Duke showed up early in the morning. We went in the parlor and sat there, and he looked so nice. My mother told me, he's a fine-looking man. He was, too. Duke was a handsome man.

And he explained to her, an opportunity was opening up at the Gateway for me as a musician international, going over there and all like that. And he explained, and I'll never forget what she said. She said, well, Howard is agrown man now and he's able to make his own decisions. And whatever he says, I'll abide by. Right then and there, I made up my mind I wasn't going to leave her.

So I told -- when she said that, she put it on me and I was giving it to her. I told Duke -- we went to the door and Duke grabbed me by the shoulder and shook my hand, he says, Scottie, I sympathize with you. I think you made a right decision. He told me that. I never forgot him for that, boy. He was crazy about his mother. And when I said that,
he says, I think you made a right decision, patted me on the back.

That was great of him. Well, the same thing happened. I felt kind of bad that -- I felt good that Duke had told me that, and he -- I left him in a different manner that I left Fletcher. See, he shook my hand and patted me on the back. But Fletcher, I just left him.
